wolf.tip: Approach slowly, with food, and do not pretend you are not afraid. Wolves respect honesty.
wolf.line: Grey and unhurried, watching you from between the trees like a question.
slips: The wolf holds your eye a long moment, then turns and is simply gone between the trees.
The wolf circles once at a distance, decides the day is not this day, and lopes off.
The wolf lifts its head, scents the air past you, and melts back into the thicket.

cat.tip: Cats choose you, not the other way around. Sit down and pretend you came for the view.
cat.line: A wood-cat, lean and self-possessed, doing an excellent impression of not having seen you.
slips: The cat blinks slowly, stands, stretches every joint it owns, and walks away mid-sentence.
The cat watches you from the log with complete comprehension and zero interest.
The cat lets you get within an arm's length and then is somehow forty feet up a tree.

owl.tip: Owls bond through patience and respect. Lower your voice and take the long way in.
owl.line: Round-eyed on a low branch, turning its whole head to keep you exactly where it wants you.
slips: The owl regards you for a long unblinking while, then lifts off without a single sound.
The owl closes its eyes, which is somehow the most complete refusal in the wood.
The owl shuffles one branch higher and resumes ignoring you from a better seat.

rabbit.tip: Easy to befriend and quick to startle. Kneel, hold something green, and let it come to you.
rabbit.line: Ears up, nose going, one back foot already deciding about the hedgerow.
slips: The rabbit freezes, reconsiders its whole morning, and bolts for the hedgerow.
The rabbit lets you get almost close enough and then is a white tail in the bracken.
The rabbit thumps once - a message, and not for you - and vanishes.

hawk.tip: Hawks respect stillness and a steady eye. Do not reach; be a place worth landing.
hawk.line: Mantled on a dead branch against the sky, and it has already counted everything in the clearing, including you.
slips: The hawk opens its wings without hurry and rows away over the treetops.
The hawk screams once - at the sky, not at you - and rides a thermal out of the story.
The hawk watches your outstretched arm with what can only be called professional scepticism, then leaves.

squirrel.tip: Easy to befriend, impossible to impress. Hazelnuts help. Guard your pockets.
squirrel.line: Upside down on a trunk, tail flagging, holding something it definitely just stole.
slips: The squirrel takes the berry right out of your open hand and bolts up the nearest oak with it.
The squirrel scolds you at length from a branch - a whole speech - and departs.
The squirrel spirals round the trunk and out of sight, still chewing.

raven.tip: Ravens are curious and keep accounts. Offer something shiny and speak to it like it understands, because it does.
raven.line: Black as spilled ink, head cocked, plainly assessing whether you are interesting or merely tall.
slips: The raven says something in raven - it does not sound flattering - and flaps off.
The raven hops exactly one hop out of reach, and will do so forever.
The raven takes off, circles you once as if memorising your face for later, and goes.

hedgehog.tip: The gentlest yes in the wood. Move slow, sit low, and wait for the ball to unroll.
hedgehog.line: A small opinionated pincushion shuffling through the leaf litter like it pays rent here.
slips: The hedgehog rolls up. That is the whole answer, and it is final.
The hedgehog trundles off under a bramble at a pace that somehow still outdistances you.
The hedgehog sniffs your fingers, huffs, and resumes its rounds without you.

badger.tip: Badgers keep old roads and old grudges. Stay off the sett path, keep your voice low, and bring something worth the interruption.
badger.line: Broad and striped and entirely unimpressed, pausing on a path its family has walked for three hundred years.
slips: The badger looks straight through you and continues down its ancestral road as if you were weather.
The badger snorts once and backs into the dark of the sett, closing the subject.
The badger takes the long way around you - not afraid, just declining the acquaintance.
